note: Painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy treated with NGF-neutralising antibodies (tanezumab, fulranumab, MEDI7352); every DPN trial was truncated by the 2010 FDA anti-NGF clinical hold, so patient data are small and short.
label: Diabetic neuropathy (anti-NGF)

engagement.model: In-vitro NGF binding and TrkA/p75 blocking assays
engagement.note: Tanezumab bound human NGF below 10 pM and blocked TrkA/p75 in vitro; no model-to-patient engagement comparison was published for DPN.
engagement.short: Sub-10 pM NGF binding in vitro
engagement.quote: Our measurements were consistent with the NGF/tanezumab binding affinity being tighter than 10 pM due to the formation of an extremely stable complex that had an estimated half-life exceeding 100 h
engagement.judgement: Quote is the first 30 words of a 41-word sentence (verbatim, truncated). Patient-side engagement was measured but never compared with a model prediction: in NCT01087203 serum total NGF rose from ~46 to ~4,194 pg/mL by week 8 on tanezumab 20 mg SC (results posted 2021-02-24), and MEDI7352 raised total NGF dose-dependently in PDN patients (Zhang 2026, doi:10.1016/j.jpba.2026.117760). No animal occupancy or total-NGF prediction was published for this class in DPN, so the cell stays untested.

efficacy.model: Rat chronic constriction injury (CCI) neuropathic pain
efficacy.note: Local anti-NGF eradicated heat and cold hyperalgesia in CCI rats: first anti-NGF use in a nerve-injury pain model.
efficacy.short: Anti-NGF cleared hyperalgesia in CCI rats
efficacy.quote: A high-dose of anti-NGF (1800 ng) was found to eradicate heat and cold hyperalgesia during postoperative days 16-28 and from days 8 to 34 after CCI, respectively.
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level reading. Polyclonal anti-NGF given locally, not a clinical product; included because it is the earliest anti-NGF antibody use in a rodent neuropathic-pain model that the later mAb programs cite.

efficacy.model: STZ-diabetic rat, spinal nerve ligation and CCI allodynia
efficacy.note: Neutralising anti-NGF reversed established tactile allodynia in STZ-diabetic rats and nerve-ligation models, the disease-matched model for painful DPN.
efficacy.quote: In the complete Freund's adjuvant-induced hind-paw inflammation, spinal nerve ligation and streptozotocin-induced neuropathic pain models, a single intraperitoneal injection of a polyclonal anti-NGF antibody reversed established tactile allodynia from approximately day 3 to day 7 after treatment.
efficacy.judgement: Second untested entry added because the model changed: this is the first use of the streptozotocin-diabetic rat (disease-matched) for anti-NGF antibodies, and it tested reversal of established pain rather than prevention. Abstract-level; polyclonal and mouse mAb, not tanezumab/fulranumab/MEDI7352.

efficacy.model: STZ-diabetic rat and nerve-injury allodynia models
efficacy.note: Fulranumab 10 mg cut DPN pain 1.2 points vs placebo with a dose-response, as rodent models predicted; tanezumab 2015 and MEDI7352 2024 agreed.
efficacy.quote: This study provides Class I evidence that in patients with DPNP, fulranumab 10 mg reduces pain by 1.2 points on an 11-point scale compared with placebo.
efficacy.reason: Rodent allodynia reversal matched DPN pain
efficacy.judgement: Status call: the trial paper reports the patient result the rodent models predicted (direction only); the paper itself does not put model and patient side by side (full text not retrievable from PMC/Europe PMC; abstract-level), so comparison_stated is false, as in the house CF/STRIVE example. Trial NCT00993018 (77 of 200 planned; stopped by the FDA hold) has no posted results, hence registry_date null. Confirmations: tanezumab 20 mg SC in NCT01087203 (Bramson 2015, doi:10.1111/pme.12677, abstract only, paywalled) week-8 pain P=0.009, registry week-16 LS mean difference -1.22 (95% CI -2.28 to -0.16, P=0.025; results posted 2021-02-24); MEDI7352 NCT03755934 high dose -1.39 (P=0.0009) and low dose -1.96 (P=0.044) but medium dose +0.72 (n.s.) at week 12 (results posted 2024-09-19; terminated for slow enrolment; no peer-reviewed efficacy paper found). No anti-NGF failed on efficacy in DPN, so no neg. product_in_model false: the rodent papers used polyclonal or mouse anti-NGF, not fulranumab.

safety.note: Anti-NGF antiserum destroyed sympathetic ganglia in newborn rodents: the class's standing neuronal-safety flag, later extended to adult rats and monkeys.
safety.quote: Destruction of the sympathetic ganglia in mammals by an antiserum to a nerve-growth protein.
safety.judgement: No abstract exists for this 1960 PNAS paper (PMC222845 is a scan); the quote is the verbatim title. Opens the strip because this antiserum result is the origin of the sympathetic-neuron safety prediction that every anti-NGF program and the FDA's December 2012 hold relied on.

safety.model: Adult cynomolgus monkey sympathetic ganglia (stereology, telemetry, tilt)
safety.note: Adult monkeys on tanezumab showed reversible neuron shrinkage, no cell death and normal sympathetic function, agreeing with patients; joint toxicity was never modelled.
safety.quote: These results agree with results from clinical studies of tanezumab indicating no evidence of sympathetic dysfunction
safety.reason: Sympathetic flag cleared; joint harm unmodelled
safety.judgement: This is the sympathetic-neuron question only, and it is the one safety comparison a primary source states outright (full text read, open access). Caveats: (1) the patient side Belanger cites is tanezumab OA/CLBP trial data (Brown 2014, doi:10.1016/j.jns.2014.07.028, is an OA study), not DPN; the DPN trials themselves reported only that neuropathy assessments (NIS, IENF density, QST) showed no meaningful change and no new safety concern despite pre-existing neuropathy (Bramson 2015), in ~150 patients over <=16 weeks. (2) The class's defining safety failure is not in this strip because no DPN-patient source exists for it: animal toxicology never flagged joints, yet rapidly progressive OA/osteonecrosis appeared in OA patients and triggered the June 2010 partial hold that halted both DPN trials (Hochberg 2016, doi:10.1002/art.39492: 'Unexpected adverse events (AEs) described as osteonecrosis (ON) occurred during tanezumab development, leading the US Food and Drug Administration to impose a partial clinical hold for all indications except cancer pain'). In DPN patients Wang 2014 reports 'No cases of joint replacement or death were reported.' A scorer who treats the joint miss as class-wide rather than context-bound would call this cell contra; by the brief's context rule and no-stretch rule it is recorded here as same with the miss documented. (3) The rodent neuron-count data behind the December 2012 hold are reinterpreted by this paper as under-recognition, not death; the 2015 hold lift preceded publication. model_filed null: the FDA 2021 tanezumab briefing document (OA BLA 761130) could not be fetched (404) and no DPN filing exists.
